text: Let’s test the impact of midhaul transport latency on our peak uplink throughput. This helps us decide how far the O-DU can be from the O-CU in our 5G deployment. First, we’ll run a 3-minute full-buffer UDP upload to get the baseline data. Then, we’ll use an impairment emulator to add midhaul delay in 1000-microsecond steps. If the throughput stays steady, we’ll keep increasing the latency. Once we see a drop, we’ll switch to 250-microsecond increments for more precision. We’ll stop the test once the uplink throughput has dropped by 30%. For every latency step, I want to record the L1 and application layer throughput every second. I’ll also monitor the PDCP layer to see if it has trouble with the added round-trip time. It’s important to verify that the RLC and MAC layers still work fine with the extra midhaul delay. I’ll plot a graph of the UDP uplink throughput versus the total midhaul latency. We also need to repeat this with TCP traffic since it’s much more sensitive to delay. The report should document the hardware and software versions of both the O-DU and O-CU. I’ll include a detailed table with all the latency values and their corresponding upload speeds. This data is vital for planning our centralized O-CU architecture. We need to ensure that user uploads aren't ruined by the network design. Finally, I’ll perform a gap analysis against our system's performance targets.

text: Let’s test the 'Position Service Accuracy' for a stationary 5G user in an indoor environment. This is a key URLLC use case for tracking assets in a warehouse or office. I want the accuracy to be as high as possible, targeting the values in ITU-R M.2410-0. We’ll conduct the test in excellent radio conditions with a SINR above 25 dB. First, we’ll trigger a location request and record the reported coordinates. Then, we’ll measure the physical distance to the real location to find the accuracy error. We’ll repeat this measurement 100 times to get a reliable statistical average. I also want to measure the Position Service Latency for each of these requests. We’ll record the time from the request to the final coordinate delivery in seconds. I want to monitor the jitter in the coordinate updates to ensure they don't jump around. On the gNB side, we’ll track the signaling load for the positioning protocol. The report should include the median error and the 95th percentile accuracy. We’ll document the UE-side RSRP and SINR for every single measurement. If the error is too high, we’ll check the multi-path interference in the room. We should also repeat this in fair and poor radio conditions to see the impact. I want to compile all these results into a clear KPI table for our URLLC assessment. This will prove our network can accurately track assets indoors. Finally, I’ll perform a gap analysis against our target accuracy goals.
